statement.p: Determine whether the vector field is conservative and, if so, find the general potential function.
Note: if the vector field is not conservative, write "DNE".

static.solution:
\mathbf{F} satisfies the cross partials condition: \begin{array}{l}\frac{\partial F_1}{\partial y}=\frac{\partial }{\partial y}( \cos z )=0\\ \frac{\partial F_2}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial }{\partial x}( 2 y^{13} )=0\end{array} \quad\Rightarrow\quad \frac{\partial F_1}{\partial y}=\frac{\partial F_2}{\partial x} \begin{array}{rcl}\frac{\partial F_2}{\partial z}=\frac{\partial }{\partial z}( 2 y^{13} )=0\\ \frac{\partial F_3}{\partial y}=\frac{\partial }{\partial y}( -x \sin z )=0\end{array} \Rightarrow \frac{\partial F_2}{\partial z}=\frac{\partial F_3}{\partial y}\begin{array}{rcl}\frac{\partial F_3}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial }{\partial x}( -x \sin z )=- \sin z\\ \frac{\partial F_1}{\partial z}=\frac{\partial }{\partial z}( \cos z )=- \sin z\end{array} \Rightarrow \frac{\partial F_3}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial F_1}{\partial z} We see that the conditions are satisfied, therefore \mathbf{F} is conservative. We find the general potential function for \mathbf{F}.
Step 1. Use the condition \frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial x}= F_1.
\varphi ( x,y,z ) is an antiderivative of F_1= \cos z when y and z are fixed, therefore: \varphi ( x,y,z )=\int \cos z \,dx=x \cos z+g( y,z ) \quad \mathbf{(1)} Step 2. Use the condition \frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial y}= F_2.
Using \mathbf{(1)} we get: \frac{\partial }{\partial y}\left(x \cos z+g( y,z )\right) = 2 y^{13} g_y(y,z) = 2 y^{13} We integrate with respect to y, holding z fixed: g(y,z)=\int 2 y^{13} \,dy= \frac1{7} \cdot y^{14} + g(z) Substituting in \mathbf{(1)} gives \varphi(x,y,z)=x \cos z+ \frac{y^{14}}{7}+g(z)\quad \mathbf{(2)} Step 3. Use the condition \frac{\partial \varphi }{\partial z}= F_3.
By \mathbf{(2)} we have \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\left(x \cos z+ \frac{y^{14}}{7}+g(z)\right) = -x \sin z -x \sin z+ g'(z) = -x \sin z g'(z) = 0\quad\Rightarrow\quad g(z)=c Substituting in \mathbf{(2)} we obtain the general potential function: \varphi ( x,y,z )=x \cos z+ \frac{y^{14}}{7}+c
